title: ArchitectureIQ: On the Measure of Training Intuition
abstract: arXiv:2609.39714v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Top researchers have good intuition, but do language models have as good intuition about model training as top AI researchers? To measure model intuition of LLMs and humans, we introduce the ArchitectureIQ benchmark. Each question presents a synthetic dataset and several training recipes, and the test-taker is asked to predict the recipe yielding the best test metric. Overall, we find that LLMs' model intuition is good but has four limitations: (1) The intuition is imperfect, or even sub-human in some cases. Frontier models achieve around 76% accuracy (random choice 33%) vs best human researcher (66.0%), yet remain far from perfect. For architecture-only questions, best human achieves 65% while GPT-6 Astra only has 38%. (2) The intuition is empirical, not structured, supported by the fact that more CoT compute does not lead to substantial improvement. Unlike math, we still lack a "Science of AI" language that enables structured reasoning

translated_abstract: 顶尖研究者拥有良好的直觉，但语言模型对模型训练的直觉是否与顶级AI研究者一样好？为了测量大语言模型和人类的模型直觉，我们提出了ArchitectureIQ基准。每个问题呈现一个合成数据集和若干训练方案，测试者需要预测哪种方案能带来最佳的测试指标。总体而言，我们发现大语言模型的模型直觉是好的，但存在四个局限：(1) 这种直觉并不完美，在某些情况下甚至低于人类水平。前沿模型达到约76%的准确率（随机选择为33%），而最佳人类研究者为66.0%，但前沿模型仍远未达到完美。对于仅涉及架构的问题，最佳人类研究者达到65%，而GPT-6 Astra只有38%。(2) 这种直觉是经验性的、而非结构化的，证据是更多的思维链（CoT）计算并不能带来实质性提升。与数学不同，我们仍然缺乏一门能够支持结构化推理的“AI科学”语言。
tldr: 该论文提出了用于测量大语言模型与人类对模型训练直觉能力的ArchitectureIQ基准，发现前沿LLM虽然直觉不错（约76%准确率）但不完美、有时甚至逊于人类专家，且这种直觉是经验性而非结构化的，增加思维链计算也无法带来实质提升。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces ArchitectureIQ, a benchmark measuring LLMs' and humans' intuition about model training, finding that while frontier models achieve good (~76%) accuracy in predicting the best training recipe, their intuition remains imperfect—sometimes sub-human—and empirical rather than structured, since additional chain-of-thought compute yields no substantial improvement.
